title: THE SISTER WHO STOOD AND WATCHED

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "His sister stood at a distance to see what would happen to him." - Exodus 2:4 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
One short verse, easy to skip. A young girl standing at a distance, watching a basket drift among the reeds, not knowing what would happen next.

She could do nothing. She could not steer the basket or control who found it. She could only stay and watch.

Some of us are living in that verse right now. We are watching a child make choices we cannot change, watching a loved one's health decline, watching a situation drift where we have no power to intervene. Standing at a distance is one of the hardest places to stand.

But notice — she stayed. She did not walk away in despair. And because she was still there when the moment came, God used her within minutes to reunite the baby with his own mother.

Your waiting is not passive. Staying present, staying prayerful, staying ready — that is faithfulness too. Mary and the women stood watching at the cross when they could do nothing (Jn 19:25), and they were the first to see the resurrection.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What am I watching that I cannot control?
2. Am I staying near in prayer, or drifting away in discouragement?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, when all I can do is watch and wait, keep me from despair. Hold me near until I see what You will do. Amen.
